name: Why is specialized drywall primer necessary before painting a newly finished addition?

mainEntity.name: Why is specialized drywall primer necessary before painting a newly finished addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drywall primers and standard interior paints serve entirely different purposes, and skipping primer can ruin the final wall finish. New drywall consists of porous paper and highly absorbent joint compound. If you apply standard paint directly, the wall absorbs moisture unevenly, resulting in a splotchy, dull appearance known as flashing. A dedicated PVA or drywall sealer seals the porous paper and mud evenly, creating a uniform surface that ensures topcoat paint adheres properly and maintains a consistent sheen.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drywall primer seals porous joint compound and raw paper, preventing uneven paint absorption, blotchy patches, and visible sheen differences across finished seams.
